groups.doc: What every page needs: a stage on a canvas, the world of blobs it draws, the camera, and the bones that move them. Start here.

groups.doc: Moves written by hand, poses mixed together, feet that find the ground, loose parts that swing after the body, and morphs.

groups.title: Simulation

props.name: morphs

entries.name: PickedBone

props.name: bone

props.name: label
props.doc: Its name for people: 'left forearm'.

props.name: blobs

props.name: offscreen
props.doc:
Draws into a render target and copies each frame to a 2D canvas on request: headless test browsers can render
WebGPU but not show it.

props.name: lights
props.doc: Builds each world with live lights (`setLights`), as Scan Studio does.

props.name: shadowDensity
props.doc: How dark what stands in a casting light's way makes it (the world's `shadowDensity`): left out, soft shadows that thin things let light through.

props.name: webgl
props.doc: Uses the WebGL 2 backend even where WebGPU would start: for testing the fallback.

props.name: cleanCuts
props.doc: Builds each world so cuts (`setEdits`) have a clean edge, tested per pixel (`setCleanCuts` turns it off and on).

entries.name: Stage
entries.doc:
The engine's front door: one rigged creature (or a scene) on a canvas, drawn
by `SplatWorld` through three.js's WebGPU renderer, which falls back to
WebGL 2 where a browser has no WebGPU. Every blob is moved by its bones on
the GPU, so a creature can have hundreds of thousands. It plays a clip or a
poser, orbits, picks bones, draws pixel art and bakes sprite sheets.

  const stage = await Stage.start(canvas)
  stage.setActor(makeFox(20000), recordClip('trot', ...))

On blobscape.dev it is the Creature page's view (`CreatureStage`) and every
engine experiment's.

`offscreen` draws into a render target and copies each frame to a 2D canvas
on request: headless test browsers can render WebGPU but not show it.

props.name: renderer
props.doc: The three.js renderer the stage made and draws with.

props.name: backend
props.doc: Which backend the renderer started on: WebGPU, or WebGL 2 where a browser has none.

props.name: orbit
props.doc: Where the camera looks from. Set it to move the view.

props.name: playing
props.doc: Whether time moves on. False holds the pose.

props.name: speed
props.doc: How fast time runs: 1 is real time, 0.5 half speed.

props.name: step
props.doc:
Held frames: above 0, the pose only moves on every `step` seconds and the picture is left alone in between,
like animation drawn at a few frames a second. In pixel mode that is what stops edges crawling.

props.name: onFirstFrame
props.doc: Called once, after the first frame with a creature in it has been drawn.

props.name: mode
props.doc: How a blob on several bones takes its shape: see `SkinMode`. Change it with `setMode`.

props.name: blobCount
props.doc: How many blobs the creature shown has.

props.name: sortKind
props.doc: Which depth sort the world uses: the counting sort, or the exact radix sort (slower; ties always in one order).

props.name: time
props.doc: Seconds into the clip, or the time a poser is showing.

props.name: artSize
props.doc: Pixel mode's art size in pixels, once a frame has been drawn.

methods.name: start
methods.doc: Starts a stage on a canvas: makes the renderer (WebGPU, or WebGL 2 where there is none) and begins drawing.

methods.name: setActor
methods.doc: Shows a creature, replacing the last one, and plays `clip` on it.

methods.name: tint
methods.doc:
Shows the actor in other colors without changing it: `paint` gives each blob's color (sRGB, 0–1) from its own and
its place in the list, and may give a fourth number, a share of the blob's own opacity (0 hides it). Left out,
its own colors come back. It stays through a new actor, until it is taken off; `highlight` and `refresh` send the
actor's own colors again, so call it again after them, and take it off before `bake`.

signatures.code: tint(paint?: (color: readonly [number, number, number], blob: number) => readonly number[]): void

methods.name: setSort
methods.doc:
Changes how blobs are sorted by depth: 'bins' is quick, 'radix' settles every tie the same way each frame, which
pixel art with hard edges wants.

methods.name: setClip
methods.doc: Plays another clip on the creature shown, or none. `from` is the time it starts at, in seconds (left out, time runs on).

methods.name: setAfter
methods.doc:
Runs `after` each time the creature is posed, once its clip or poser has set the bones and before loose parts
swing: for a change laid on top of any move, such as a head turned to look at something. It must leave the
skeleton updated. It stays through a new clip and goes with a new actor.

signatures.code: setAfter(after?: (sk: Skeleton, t: number) => void): void

methods.name: setPoser
methods.doc: Poses from the time instead of a clip; `t` starts at `from` seconds.

signatures.code: setPoser(poser?: (sk: Skeleton, t: number) => void, from?: number): void

methods.name: setSwing
methods.doc: Loose parts that swing after the body while a move plays (a `Swing` made for this actor's skeleton), or none.

signatures.code: setSwing(swing?: { update: any; reset: any }): void

methods.name: setMorphWeights
methods.doc: The morphs' weights while no clip keys them (the clip's own weights win while it plays).

methods.name: refresh
methods.doc: After the actor's blobs were changed in place (a poser may do it each frame): the engine takes them again.

methods.name: setMode
methods.doc: Changes how a blob on several bones takes its shape: see `SkinMode`.

methods.name: setFog
methods.doc: Distance fog toward `color` (linear) from `near` to `far` units from the camera (`far` 0 is none); kept for the next actor too.

signatures.code: setFog(color: [number, number, number], near: number, far: number): void

methods.name: setEdits
methods.doc:
Cuts by shape, live (edit.ts): spheres, boxes or upright cylinders in world space, kept for the next actor too;
[] clears them. On a stage made with `cleanCuts` the edge is the shape's own line.

methods.name: setCleanCuts
methods.doc: On a stage made with `cleanCuts`: whether cuts have the clean edge (the default) or drop whole blobs.

methods.name: setOutline
methods.doc:
Draws outlines over the picture as a pen would (inkLines.ts): round the subject, where one thing stands in front
of another, and between its parts. Leave the pen out to stop. With any look, or none; pixel mode has its own lines.

methods.name: setMarks
methods.doc:
Draws every blob as a brush mark or an ink stroke, or as soft dots again when left out; kept for the next actor
too. The marks belong to the blobs, so they stay put as the view turns.

methods.name: setLights
methods.doc:
Live lights on the world (needs the `lights` option); kept for the next actor too. A light is at a place or from a
direction (a sun); `ambient` is one brightness or a linear color.

signatures.code: setLights(lights: Light[], ambient?: number | readonly [number, number, number]): void

methods.name: setFloor
methods.doc: A floor `size` across in half-unit squares, so the grid shows how big each creature is.

methods.name: setShow
methods.doc: Shows the blobs, the bones, or both.

methods.name: setPixels
methods.doc:
Pixel mode on (with a look) or off. `size` is how many CSS pixels across
one art pixel is; the art is that many times smaller than the view.

methods.name: pixelFrames
methods.doc: Pixel mode's last frame as it was drawn small, and as finished art (exactly in the look's colors): for tests and for saving.

signatures.code: pixelFrames(): Promise<{ small: Frame; art: Frame; before?: Frame; parts?: Frame; fine?: { small: Frame; parts: Frame } } | undefined>

methods.name: pick
methods.doc:
The bone under a point on the view (CSS pixels from its top left), as the creature stands now:
the bone that holds most of the blob the pointer is on. Undefined when the pointer is off the creature.

signatures.code: pick(x: number, y: number): PickedBone | undefined

methods.name: rayAt
methods.doc: The line from the camera through a point on the view (CSS pixels from its top left), in world space.

signatures.code: rayAt(x: number, y: number): { origin: [number, number, number]; direction: [number, number, number] } | undefined

methods.name: screenAt
methods.doc:
Where a point in world space falls on the view, in CSS pixels from its top left, for drawing over the picture;
undefined behind the camera. `orbit` is the view to use when it is not the stage's own yet.

signatures.code: screenAt(p: ArrayLike<number>, orbit?: Orbit): { x: number; y: number } | undefined

methods.name: hitAt
methods.doc: The bone under a point on the view (CSS pixels from its top left) and where the pointer meets it, in world space.

signatures.code: hitAt(x: number, y: number): { bone: number; point: [number, number, number] } | undefined

methods.name: boneInfo
methods.doc: What the page says about a bone.

methods.name: highlight
methods.doc: Lights up one bone and the blobs it moves (or none).

methods.name: invalidate
methods.doc:
Asks for the next `frames` frames to be drawn. Call it after changing something the stage can't see, such as its
`orbit`.

methods.name: frame
methods.doc: Offscreen only: draws the frame `t` seconds into the clip and copies it to the page.

methods.name: bake
methods.doc:
Draws the creature on show as a pixel-art sprite sheet (bakeSheet.ts), with
the floor and bones out of the picture and the live view paused, then puts
the view back as it was.

signatures.code: bake(moves: SheetMove[], opts: BakeOptions, progress?: (done: number, total: number) => void): Promise<BakedSheet>

methods.doc: Stops drawing and frees what the stage made.

modules.title: SplatWorld: every blob in one three.js object

entries.name: Actor
entries.doc:
Blobscape's splat engine: one mesh that draws every blob of every object in a
scene, so objects that overlap (stems in a vase, a fox in long grass) sort
against each other blob by blob, instead of object by object.

Every blob hangs on bones. A still object is one bone; a creature is a
skeleton. Each frame:

1. deform (compute): each blob's center and shape go from its rest pose to the
   world through its bones, as `skinBlob` in rig.ts does on the CPU;
2. sort (compute): every blob in the scene by depth, one counting sort;
3. draw: one instanced quad per blob, projected and shaded as in 3DGS.

It draws through three.js's WebGPURenderer, so it shares a depth buffer and a
camera with ordinary three.js meshes. On the WebGL backend the deform and sort
run on the CPU and the result is uploaded; the drawing is the same.

The projection and shading follow three.js's `GaussianSplat` (MIT), which in
turn follows the 3DGS paper; what's new here is the shared sort and skinning.

props.name: blobs
props.doc: The blobs in the rest pose.

props.name: skin
props.doc: Which bones move each blob, and by how much.

props.name: skeleton
props.doc: The bones, and their pose.

props.name: partOf
props.doc: Which part of the actor each blob belongs to (as `buildBody` and `voxelBody` give it): what `SplatWorld.parts` draws. Left out, the actor is one part.

props.name: seen
props.doc:
How much of each of the first four live lights a blob can see, four bytes a blob (255 sees it all): baked lamp
shadows (voxel.ts `lamps`). The light pass scales light k by byte k, so a flickering lamp's shadows flicker with it.
Left out, every light reaches every blob.

props.name: glow
props.doc:
How much of its own light each blob gives, a byte a blob (255 all of it): a lit window, a firefly, the moon. Under
live lights such a blob is never drawn darker than this share of its own color, so it stays bright when the scene
goes dark. Left out, nothing glows.

props.name: morphs
props.doc: Blend shapes (morph.ts), set with `SplatWorld.setMorphWeights`: on WebGPU a pass before the deform reshapes the blobs; on WebGL the CPU does and uploads them.

entries.name: MAX_MORPH_TARGETS
entries.doc: How many morph targets a world takes, over all its actors.

entries.name: EngineOptions
entries.doc:
How a `SplatWorld` is built: its sort, how a blob on several bones turns, and whether it lights or paints its
blobs.

props.name: bins
props.doc: Depth buckets for the counting sort. More buckets, fewer ties between blobs that are close in depth.

props.name: sort
props.doc:
'bins' (the default): a counting sort over `bins` depth buckets, small buckets settled into index order.
'radix': a stable radix sort over 2²⁴ depth steps (radix.ts), every tie in index order however many share it.

props.name: mode
props.doc: How a blob on several bones takes its shape ('quat' unless set): see `SkinMode`.

props.name: lights
props.doc: Live lights (`setLights`): each blob is lit every frame from its normal. Off unless asked for, as it costs a pass.

props.name: shadowDensity
props.doc:
How dark what stands in a casting light's way makes it (`SHADOW_DENSITY`, 1.5, where left out): low, a shadow is
soft and thin things let light through; about 5, a wall one blob thick blocks nearly all of it, which suits solid
scenes under a sun.

props.name: paint
props.doc: Paint edits (`setEdits` with op 'paint'): needs the same color pass as lights. Cuts work without it.

props.name: cleanCuts
props.doc:
Cuts with a clean edge: a blob a cut passes through is kept and each of its pixels is tested against the cut,
so the edge is the shape's own line and not a row of whole blobs. Costs the draw a test per pixel while there are
edits; `cleanCuts` on the world turns it off and on again.

entries.name: PointLight
entries.doc: A point light for `setLights`.

props.name: position
props.doc: Where it is, in world space.

props.name: color
props.doc: Linear RGB, times its strength: [1, 0.6, 0.3] is a torch at full strength.

props.name: range
props.doc: Its reach: about a quarter strength at this distance, and gone by twice it.

props.name: shadow
props.doc: Whether it casts shadows (`shadow.ts`): blobs between a blob and the light take some of it. Off unless set.

entries.name: SunLight
entries.doc:
A light from one direction that reaches everything, for `setLights`: the sun, or the moon. It doesn't fade with
distance, and its shadows (with `shadow`) fall the same way everywhere.

props.name: direction
props.doc: The way toward the light from anywhere in the scene (any length but zero): [0, 1, 0] is straight overhead.

props.name: color
props.doc: Linear RGB, times its strength: [1.1, 1, 0.9] is a midday sun.

props.name: shadow
props.doc: Whether it casts shadows (`shadow.ts`). Off unless set.

entries.name: Light
entries.doc: A light `setLights` takes: one at a place, or one from a direction.

entries.name: MAX_LIGHTS
entries.doc: How many lights `setLights` takes; the rest are dropped.

entries.name: SplatWorld
entries.doc:
Every blob of every actor as one three.js mesh, so things that overlap are sorted against each other in one pass.
On WebGPU the bones move the blobs, and the blobs are projected and sorted, in compute passes each frame; on WebGL
2 the vertex shader moves them and the CPU sorts. Add it to a scene drawn by three.js's `WebGPURenderer`, or let
`Stage` do that for you.

props.name: isSplatWorld
props.doc: Marks the object as a `SplatWorld`, the way three.js marks its own kinds.

props.name: count
props.doc: How many blobs it holds, over every actor.

props.name: actors
props.doc: The actors it was built from.

props.name: boneCount
props.doc: How many bones it holds, over every actor.

props.name: mode
props.doc: How a blob on several bones takes its shape: see `SkinMode`.

props.name: cpuPath
props.doc: Set by the WebGL backend path, read by tests: did the last frame skin on the CPU?

props.name: cpuMs
props.doc: Milliseconds the CPU spent in the last frame (WebGL path only): moving centers, sorting, both.

props.name: cpuSkinMs
props.doc: Milliseconds of that spent moving centers.

props.name: cpuSortMs
props.doc: Milliseconds of that spent sorting.

props.name: hold
props.doc: While true, rendering draws the last frame's blobs without moving or sorting them (for timing the draw alone, and for a second draw of the same frame such as the map of parts).

props.name: parts
props.doc:
While true, the draw is a map of parts, not a picture: every blob is a hard disc in its part's own flat color
(red and green hold the part's number plus one, blue the actor's), with no light, fog or soft edge, so where two
parts meet the color changes exactly. Pixel mode draws it for the lines between parts.

props.name: depthMap
props.doc:
While true, the draw is a depth map: every blob a hard disc (as in the map of parts) whose color is its distance in
front of the camera, in units, in all three channels. Drawn after the frame's own render with `hold`, the frame's
sort puts the nearest disc last, so each pixel keeps the nearest depth. `SplatDepth` (depth.ts) draws it.

props.name: autoDetail
props.doc:
Level of detail: while set, each actor draws a share of its blobs by how big it is on screen (`detailFor`),
the rest grown to cover for them. Off (every blob drawn) unless asked for; turning it off draws every blob again.

props.name: bounds
props.doc: A sphere round every actor's posed bones, for placing a camera or a shadow grid.

props.name: fog
props.doc:
Distance fog: blobs fade toward `color` (linear RGB) from `near` to `far`
in front of the camera, so a scene can end in mist instead of an edge.
Off while `far` is 0.

props.name: lighting
props.doc: Live lighting, when the world was made with `lights: true`.

props.name: cleanCuts
props.doc: Whether cuts have a clean edge now. Only a world made with `cleanCuts` can; setting it there switches between the clean edge and whole blobs.

props.name: detail
props.doc: The share of each actor's blobs being drawn.

props.name: sortKind
props.doc: Which depth sort this world was built with.

props.name: order
props.doc: The order the last sort produced (drawn first is farthest). Only up to date on the CPU path.

methods.name: setMarks
methods.doc:
Draws every blob as a brush mark or an ink stroke (marks.ts) in place of a soft dot, or as dots again when left
out. A mark is turned and stretched by its blob's own shape on screen and seeded by the blob, so it stays on its
blob as the view moves. Maps of parts and depth are drawn as before.

methods.name: setFog
methods.doc: Fades blobs to `color` (linear RGB, 0–1) between `near` and `far` units from the camera; `far` 0 turns it off.

signatures.code: setFog(color: [number, number, number], near: number, far: number): void

methods.name: setLights
methods.doc:
Lights the blobs with up to MAX_LIGHTS lights, on top of `ambient` times their own (baked) color: point lights
that fade with distance, and lights from a direction (a sun, a moon) that don't. `ambient` is one brightness or a
linear color, for light from the whole sky. Each blob's normal is its flattest axis, so a light reaches the side
of a surface that faces it. Needs `lights: true`.

signatures.code: setLights(lights: Light[], ambient?: number | readonly [number, number, number]): void

methods.name: setEdits
methods.doc:
Cuts and paints by shape, live (edit.ts): up to MAX_EDITS spheres or boxes in world space, tested against where each
blob is now. A cut blob gets no size; a painted one is mixed toward the paint before any light (needs `paint: true`
or `lights: true`). Replaces the edits before; [] clears them.

methods.name: setMorphWeights
methods.doc: Sets an actor's morph weights (one per morph, 0–1); the blobs are reshaped next frame.

signatures.code: setMorphWeights(actor: number | Actor, weights: ArrayLike<number>): void

methods.name: markPosed
methods.doc: Call after posing any skeleton.

methods.name: setDetail
methods.doc: Draws `keep` (0–1) of an actor's blobs, each grown to cover for the rest. 1 draws them all. `autoDetail` overrides it each frame.

signatures.code: setDetail(actor: number | Actor, keep: number): void

methods.name: refresh
methods.doc:
Takes the actors' blobs again after they were changed in place: centers, shapes, colors and opacities, for blobs
that something other than a bone moves (a shape shift). The counts, the bones and the weights must be as they were.

methods.name: recolor
methods.doc:
Takes one actor's colors and opacities again after they were changed in place, when nothing moved
(a floor that scorches): only the color buffer goes up again.

methods.name: checkShadows
methods.doc:
For tests: the GPU's grid of shadows against the CPU twin's, built from the CPU's deform of the same frame
(WebGPU, with a light casting). Returns the cells that differ by more than one unit and the total in each.

signatures.code: checkShadows(renderer: Renderer): Promise<{ differ: number; gpuTotal: number; cpuTotal: number }>

methods.name: stages
methods.doc:
The frame's GPU work in stages, so a timer can wait between them. Each
assumes the ones before it ran: deform (bones → world), then project
(world → screen, plus sort keys), then order (the sort itself).

signatures.code: stages(renderer: Renderer, camera: Camera): { deform: () => void; project: () => void; order: () => void }

methods.name: deformCPU
methods.doc:
The CPU twin of the deform pass: every blob's world center (4 floats) and
covariance (6). It reads the same byte weights the GPU does, so the two agree.

methods.name: checkAgainstCPU
methods.doc:
Reads back what the GPU deform wrote and compares it with the CPU twin.
Returns the largest differences in center (world units) and covariance.

signatures.code: checkAgainstCPU(renderer: Renderer): Promise<{ center: number; cov: number; covScale: number }>

methods.name: checkViewColors
methods.doc:
Reads back the colors the GPU gave each blob by angle and checks them against `viewColor` (sh.ts) for the view
last drawn: the largest gap per channel, 0–1. Only meaningful with no lights and no paint (the pass's output is
the lit color). WebGPU only.

methods.name: checkSort
methods.doc:
Reads the sorted order back from the GPU and counts what is wrong with it: blobs missing, out of order, or in
bins left unsettled. For tests.

signatures.code: checkSort(renderer: Renderer): Promise<{ missing: number; outOfOrder: number; unsettled: number; biggest: number }>

methods.name: dispose
methods.doc: Frees the GPU-related resources allocated by this instance.

modules.title: Orbit: where the camera looks from

entries.name: Orbit
entries.doc: Where the orbit camera is: it circles `target` at `distance`, looking at it.

props.name: target
props.doc: The point it looks at.

props.name: distance
props.doc: How far from the target it is.

props.name: azimuth
props.doc: Degrees around the vertical axis; 0 looks from +Z.

props.name: elevation
props.doc: Degrees above the horizon.

entries.name: FOV
entries.doc: The camera's vertical field of view, in degrees.

entries.name: STAGE_FOV
entries.doc: The vertical field of view of the engine's `Stage` camera, in degrees.

entries.name: placeCamera
entries.doc: Places a three.js camera for an orbit and a canvas aspect.

signatures.code: placeCamera(cam: PerspectiveCamera, o: Orbit, aspect: number): void

entries.name: lensOf
entries.doc: The projection of a placed camera as a `Lens`, in CSS pixels.

signatures.code: lensOf(cam: PerspectiveCamera, width: number, height: number): Lens

entries.name: orbitLens
entries.doc: A lens for an orbit without any renderer: for the software views and tests.

signatures.code: orbitLens(o: Orbit, width: number, height: number): Lens

entries.name: Blobs
entries.doc:
A list of Gaussian blobs, kept as flat typed arrays (one entry per blob) so a
scene of tens of thousands stays cheap to copy, undo and hand to the GPU.

Each blob is the five kinds of number (14 values) a 3D Gaussian splat is made of:
a center, three scales (standard deviations along its own axes), a rotation
(unit quaternion x, y, z, w), a color and an opacity. Colors are stored as
given to Spark (0–1 per channel), which draws them as sRGB.

props.name: count
props.doc: How many blobs.

props.name: center
props.doc: Centers: x, y, z per blob.

props.name: scale
props.doc: Sizes along each blob's own axes (standard deviations): three per blob.

props.name: quat
props.doc: Rotations as unit quaternions: x, y, z, w per blob.

props.name: color
props.doc: Colors, 0–1 sRGB: red, green, blue per blob.

props.name: opacity
props.doc: Opacity, 0–1: one per blob.

props.name: shDegree
props.doc:
Color by angle, when the blobs have it: `shDegree` 1–3, and per blob
`shTerms` triples (r, g, b for each spherical harmonic term after the
first, in the files' order and signs: see `viewColor` in sh.ts). Blobs
without it have degree 0 and no array.

props.name: sh
props.doc: The color-by-angle terms themselves, or null when the blobs have none: see `shDegree`.

props.name: capacity
props.doc: How many blobs the arrays have room for; they grow as blobs are pushed.

props.name: shTerms
props.doc: Rest terms per blob: 0, 3, 8 or 15.

props.name: bytes
props.doc: Bytes held by the used part, for capping undo history.

methods.name: setSHDegree
methods.doc: Gives the blobs color by angle up to `degree` (0 removes it), keeping the terms they already have.

methods.name: push
methods.doc: Adds a blob and returns its index.

methods.name: set
methods.doc: Writes blob `i`.

methods.name: get
methods.doc: Reads blob `i`.

methods.name: filter
methods.doc: Keeps the blobs where `keep(i)` is true, in order. Returns how many were removed.

methods.name: clone
methods.doc: A copy that shares nothing with this one.

entries.name: Vec3
entries.doc: Three numbers: a point or a direction (x, y, z), or a color (red, green, blue).

entries.name: Bone
entries.doc:
A skeleton: bones in a tree, each placed by its head in the rest pose (world
space, no rest rotation) and posed by a local rotation about its head plus an
optional offset. Bone 0 is usually the root; a still object in a scene is just
a skeleton of one bone.

`update()` turns the pose into what the skinning pass needs per bone: the skin
matrix (posed world × inverse rest, column-major 4×4), its rotation as a
quaternion, and its uniform scale. A bone's scale carries down to its
children, as in glTF.

props.name: name
props.doc: What poses and files call it.

props.name: parent
props.doc: The index of the bone it hangs on, or -1 for a root.

props.name: head
props.doc: Where it turns about, in the rest pose.

props.name: tail
props.doc: Where the bone ends in the rest pose, for drawing it. A bone with children points at its first child when this is missing.

entries.name: Skeleton
entries.doc:
Bones in a tree, and their pose. Set `rotation`, `offset` and `size` (or use the posing helpers), then call
`update()` to work out what the skinning pass needs; `reset()` goes back to the rest pose.

props.name: bones
props.doc: The bones, parents before their children.

props.name: rotation
props.doc: Pose: local rotation per bone (x, y, z, w).

props.name: offset
props.doc: Pose: local offset per bone, added to its rest offset from the parent.

props.name: size
props.doc: Pose: local uniform scale per bone, about its head; children inherit it.

props.name: rootScale
props.doc: Pose: uniform scale of the root (bone 0), on top of its `size`.

props.name: place
props.doc: Where the actor stands: added to every root bone, and kept by `reset()` (a pose isn't a placement).

props.name: matrix
props.doc: Output, per bone: skin matrix (16), skin rotation quaternion (4), skin uniform scale (1).

props.name: quat
props.doc: Output, per bone: the skin rotation as a quaternion (4).

props.name: scale
props.doc: Output, per bone: the skin's uniform scale (1).

props.name: posedHead
props.doc: Posed world position of each bone's head, for drawing the rig.

props.name: count
props.doc: How many bones.

methods.name: index
methods.doc: A bone's index by its name. Throws when there is no such bone.

methods.name: setRotation
methods.doc: Sets one bone's local rotation (x, y, z, w).

methods.name: reset
methods.doc: Back to the rest pose.

methods.name: update
methods.doc:
Works the pose out: every bone's skin matrix, rotation and scale, parents first. Call it after posing and before
drawing.

entries.name: Skin
entries.doc: How each blob hangs on the skeleton: up to four bones and weights summing to 1.

props.name: joints
props.doc: Four bone indices per blob.

props.name: weights
props.doc: Four weights per blob, for those bones, summing to 1.

entries.name: emptySkin
entries.doc:
A skin for `count` blobs with nothing in it yet: four bone indices and four weights per blob. Fill it with
`setWeights`.

entries.name: setWeights
entries.doc: Keeps the four largest weights and makes them sum to 1.

signatures.code: setWeights(skin: Skin, i: number, pairs: [bone: number, weight: number][]): void

entries.name: packWeights
entries.doc:
Four weights to four bytes summing to exactly 255, so a blob never shrinks
or grows from rounding: normalized first (files may not be), and whatever
rounding leaves over goes to the largest weight. All zero means the first bone.

entries.name: SkinMode
entries.doc:
How a blob on several bones takes its shape: 'linear' pushes it through the blended matrices, which squashes it on
a twisting joint; 'quat' averages the bones' rotations and scales, so it only ever turns. See `skinBlob`.

entries.name: skinBlob
entries.doc:
Moves one blob by its bones. Positions blend the skin matrices linearly (as
every engine does). The blob's shape then follows one of two rules:

- 'linear': its covariance is pushed through the blended 3×3 matrix. A blend of
  two rotations is not a rotation, so a blob on a twisting joint gets squashed.
- 'quat': its rotation is the weighted average of the bone rotations
  (quaternions sign-aligned, summed, renormalized) and its scale the weighted
  average scale, so the blob only ever turns, never flattens.

Writes the world center (3) and covariance [xx, xy, xz, yy, yz, zz] (6).

signatures.code: skinBlob(center: ArrayLike<number>, scale: ArrayLike<number>, quat: ArrayLike<number>, joints: ArrayLike<number>, weights: ArrayLike<number>, rig: { matrix: ArrayLike<number>; quat: ArrayLike<number>; scale: ArrayLike<number> }, mode: SkinMode, outCenter: Float32Array, oc: number, outCov: Float32Array, ov: number): void

entries.name: norm4
entries.doc: A quaternion scaled to unit length.

entries.name: mulQ
entries.doc: The product of two quaternions: the turn `b`, then the turn `a`.

entries.name: axisAngle
entries.doc: The quaternion for a turn of `rad` radians about `axis`.

entries.name: rotate
entries.doc: A vector turned by a quaternion.

entries.name: quatMat3
entries.doc: Row-major 3×3 rotation of a unit quaternion.

entries.name: skinCenters
entries.doc:
Moves only the centers of many blobs, fast: what the sort needs on the CPU
when the GPU does the rest of the skinning. No allocation per blob.

- `src`: rest centers as vec4s, with each blob's first bone (its actor's
  offset into `bones`) in w;
- `skin`: two words per blob, four joint bytes then four weight bytes summing to 255;
- `bones`: 20 floats per bone, the first 16 its column-major skin matrix.

Writes xyz into `out` (3 floats per blob). Matches `skinBlob`'s center.

signatures.code: skinCenters(src: Float32Array, skin: Uint32Array, bones: Float32Array, count: number, out: Float32Array): void

entries.name: posedPoint
entries.doc: A point carried by bone `bone`'s current pose: where its rest position `p` has moved to.

signatures.code: posedPoint(sk: { matrix: ArrayLike<number> }, bone: number, p: ArrayLike<number>): [number, number, number]

modules.title: Posing by hand
modules.doc:
Small helpers for writing clips by hand, the way an animator thinks: aim a
bone at a direction, ease in and out of a move, hold a pose for a while.
Clips are functions of time that pose a skeleton; `recordClip` turns them
into keys for a file.

entries.name: X
entries.doc: The x axis.

entries.name: Y
entries.doc: The y axis: up.

entries.name: Z
entries.doc: The z axis.

entries.name: ramp
entries.doc: 0 → 1 smoothly as t goes from a to b.

signatures.code: ramp(t: number, a: number, b: number): number

entries.name: env
entries.doc: Up from a to b, held, then down from c to d.
entries.type: (t: number, a: number, b: number, c: number, d: number) => number

entries.name: conj
entries.doc: A unit quaternion's inverse: the same turn, the other way.

entries.name: fromTo
entries.doc: The rotation that turns unit vector a onto unit vector b by the shortest way.

entries.name: worldQuat
entries.doc: A bone's world rotation from the local rotations set so far (bones have no rest rotation, so it's the product up the chain).

entries.name: dir
entries.doc: A vector scaled to length 1.

entries.name: restDir
entries.doc: Where a bone points in the rest pose.

entries.name: aim
entries.doc:
Turns bone `name` so it points along world direction `to`, blended by
`amount` from where it points now. Set parents first: the result is a local
rotation under whatever the parent is doing.

signatures.code: aim(sk: Skeleton, name: string, to: Vec3, amount?: number): void

entries.name: turn
entries.doc: Adds a local turn on top of a bone's current rotation.

signatures.code: turn(sk: Skeleton, name: string, axis: Vec3, rad: number): void

entries.name: set
entries.doc: Sets a local turn, replacing the bone's rotation.

signatures.code: set(sk: Skeleton, name: string, axis: Vec3, rad: number): void

entries.name: turns
entries.doc: Several turns, applied in order (first is outermost).

entries.name: Pose

props.name: rotation
props.doc: Each bone's local rotation (x, y, z, w).

props.name: offset
props.doc: Each bone's offset from its rest place (x, y, z).

props.name: size
props.doc: Each bone's size (1 is as built).

entries.name: takePose
entries.doc: A copy of the skeleton's pose as it is now: every bone's rotation, offset and size.

entries.name: putPose
entries.doc: Sets the skeleton's pose from one taken with `takePose`. Call the skeleton's `update()` after.

entries.name: blendPose
entries.doc:
Blends from `from` to the skeleton's pose by `w` (0 leaves `from`, 1 keeps
the pose as it is). Rotations go the short way and are renormalized, which
is close to a slerp for the angles between two poses of one move.

signatures.code: blendPose(sk: Skeleton, from: Pose | Omit<Pose, "size">, w: number): void

entries.name: addPose
entries.doc:
Lays `layer` on the skeleton's pose as a change from `ref`, by `w`: each
bone turns by layer·ref⁻¹ on top of what it does now, slides by the offset's
change and grows by the size's ratio. A layer equal to `ref` changes nothing.

signatures.code: addPose(sk: Skeleton, layer: Pose, ref: Pose, w?: number): void

entries.name: MixMove
entries.doc: A move a `Mixer` can blend: its name, how long its loop takes and the function that poses it.

props.name: name
props.doc: What the mixer knows it by.

props.name: seconds
props.doc: Seconds a loop takes; the move's time wraps at it. Leave it out for a move that runs on (a pose held, or a one-off read with `elapsed`).

props.name: pose
props.doc: Poses the skeleton `t` seconds into the move.

entries.name: Mixer
entries.doc:
Plays moves and crossfades between them. `play(name, fade)` brings one move
up to full weight over `fade` seconds while every other fades out; `update(dt)`
moves the clocks and weights on; `apply(sk)` poses the skeleton as the
weighted blend. Weights always sum to 1 while anything plays, so a blend is
never a shrunken pose.

Each move keeps its own time, and `speed` scales a move's clock: a walk can
keep pace with the ground while the idle under it breathes on.

methods.name: play
methods.doc: Fades `name` in over `fade` seconds (0: at once) and everything else out. `restart` sets its clock back to 0.

signatures.code: play(name: string, fade?: number, restart?: boolean): void

methods.name: setWeights
methods.doc: Sets weights directly (they are scaled to sum to 1), as a run blends with speed. No fade.

methods.name: weight
methods.doc: How much of a move is in the mix now.

methods.name: time
methods.doc: A move's own time, in seconds since it started (wrapped by `seconds` when it loops).

methods.name: advance
methods.doc: Moves a clock on by its own amount (a walk at the pace of the feet; negative backs up).

methods.name: update
methods.doc: Moves every clock on by `dt` (times `speed[name]` where given) and every weight toward its target.

signatures.code: update(dt: number, speed?: Record<string, number>): void

methods.name: apply
methods.doc: Poses `sk` as the blend of every move with weight, in the order they were given; each move starts from the rest pose. Doesn't call `update()` on the skeleton.

modules.title: Reaching and feet on the ground
modules.doc:
Reaching for things: inverse kinematics on our skeletons, the part of a
mesh engine's animation tools (three.js's `CCDIKSolver`, a game engine's
foot IK) that creatures need most.

- `twoBoneIK` bends a limb of two bones (thigh and shin, arm and forearm)
  so its end lands on a point, keeping the knee on the side it bends now;
- `lookAt` turns one bone so a direction it carries points at a place;
- `plantFeet` lays a walk over uneven ground: hips down to the lower foot,
  each leg bent to its own patch of ground, each foot tilted to the slope;
- `hipDrop` and `stepLegs` put feet where a footstep planner (steps.ts) says.

Bones here have no rest rotation, so a bone's world turn is the product of
the local ones up its chain (`worldQuat`), and changing a bone's world turn
means setting its local turn to parent⁻¹ · wanted.

entries.name: setWorldQuat
entries.doc: Gives bone `b` the world turn `q`, under whatever its parent does now.

signatures.code: setWorldQuat(sk: Skeleton, b: number, q: ArrayLike<number>): void

entries.name: TwoBoneOptions
entries.doc: Options for `twoBoneIK`.

props.name: pole
props.doc: World direction the knee or elbow should point when the limb gives no bend of its own (it is straight).

props.name: amount
props.doc: 0 leaves the limb as it is, 1 reaches all the way.

entries.name: twoBoneIK
entries.doc:
Bends the chain upper → lower so `tip`, a point carried by `lower` (given
where it is in the rest pose: an ankle, a wrist, the end of a shin), lands on
`target`, or as near as the limb reaches. The knee stays in the plane it
bends in now, so a walk's knees keep pointing the way they did. Leaves the
skeleton updated. Returns how far the tip still is from the target.

signatures.code: twoBoneIK(sk: Skeleton, upper: number, lower: number, tip: ArrayLike<number>, target: ArrayLike<number>, options?: TwoBoneOptions): number

entries.name: LookOptions
entries.doc: Options for `lookAt`.

props.name: forward
props.doc: The direction the bone looks along at rest, in world space (a creature facing +z looks along +z).

props.name: amount
props.doc: 0 leaves the bone, 1 turns it all the way.

props.name: limit
props.doc: The most it turns from where it points now, in radians, so a head never spins round.

entries.name: lookAt
entries.doc: Turns bone `name` so its `forward` points at `point`. Leaves the skeleton updated.

signatures.code: lookAt(sk: Skeleton, name: string, point: ArrayLike<number>, options?: LookOptions): void

entries.name: Leg
entries.doc:
One leg for `plantFeet`: bone names from the hip down. The ankle is the foot
bone's head, or `tip` (a rest point the lower bone carries) for a leg with no
foot bone. `pole` is where its knee points if the leg is straight.

props.name: upper
props.doc: The thigh bone's name.

props.name: lower
props.doc: The shin bone's name.

props.name: foot
props.doc: The foot bone's name, if the leg has one.

props.name: tip
props.doc: The ankle as a rest point the lower bone carries, for a leg with no foot bone.

props.name: pole
props.doc: Where the knee points if the leg is straight.

entries.name: Ground
entries.doc: The height of the ground under a point on the floor plane.

entries.name: groundNormal
entries.doc:
The ground's way up under (x, z). Each way across is the gentler of the two
one-sided slopes, so a foot beside a step's edge stands level on its tread
instead of tipping toward the drop.

signatures.code: groundNormal(ground: Ground, x: number, z: number, e?: number): Vec3

entries.name: PlantOptions
entries.doc: Options for `plantFeet`.

props.name: amount
props.doc: 0 leaves the walk as it is (on flat ground), 1 plants it fully.

props.name: hips
props.doc: Lower the hips so the lower foot can reach (true), or leave them and let that leg hang.

props.name: tilt
props.doc: Tilt each foot to the slope under it.

entries.name: Planted
entries.doc: What `plantFeet` did, for a readout or a test.

props.name: hipShift
props.doc: How far the hips moved down (negative) or up.

props.name: legs
props.type: { target: Vec3; miss: number; ground: number }[]
props.doc: Per leg: the ankle's target and how far it ended from it.

entries.name: plantFeet
entries.doc:
Lays the pose (made for flat ground at y = 0) over `ground`. Each ankle
keeps its height above the floor from the walk (a lifted foot stays lifted),
measured from that leg's own patch of ground instead of from 0. The hips
move by the smallest of the legs' changes, so no leg has to stretch past its
length, then each leg is bent to its target and each foot turned to the
slope. Leaves the skeleton updated.

signatures.code: plantFeet(sk: Skeleton, legs: Leg[], ground: Ground, options?: PlantOptions): Planted

entries.name: hipDrop
entries.doc:
How far the hips must come down (meters, 0 or more) so every leg reaches its ankle target with a little bend
left (`slack` of its length): a long stride from straight legs needs the body lower. The skeleton as posed now.

signatures.code: hipDrop(sk: Skeleton, legs: Leg[], targets: ArrayLike<number>[], slack?: number): number

entries.name: stepLegs
entries.doc:
Bends each leg so its ankle lands on its target (from a footstep planner, say), and turns each foot bone level,
facing `facing[i]` (radians from +z toward +x) when given. Leaves the skeleton updated; returns each leg's miss.

signatures.code: stepLegs(sk: Skeleton, legs: Leg[], targets: ArrayLike<number>[], facing?: number[]): number[]

modules.title: Footsteps
modules.doc:
Footstep planning: instead of a walk clip moving the legs and the feet being pinned to the ground
after, each foot keeps a spot on the ground and only leaves it to step. A foot steps when its spot has fallen
too far from where it would stand under the body now (`reach`), aiming up to `reach` ahead of the body's motion, so
one planner walks, turns on the spot, sidesteps, backs up and stops with every foot still where it landed.
Feet in one `group` step together (a trot's diagonal pair); only one group is ever in the air, and the group
furthest behind goes first. Pure, plain numbers: the same motion gives the same steps.

entries.name: StepFoot
entries.doc: One foot for `Steps` to plan.

props.name: home
props.doc: Where the foot stands under the body at rest, in the body's frame: x to its left, z ahead.

entries.name: StepOptions
entries.doc: How `Steps` steps: how far a foot may trail, how long and how high a step is, and which feet go together.

props.name: reach
props.doc: How far a planted foot may fall from its home under the body before it steps, meters.

props.name: duration
props.doc:
Seconds a step takes in the air, at most: a body moving fast enough to cover two `reach`es in that time steps
quicker, so the feet still under it don't fall far behind before the step lands.

props.name: lift
props.doc: How high a step lifts the foot at its middle, meters.

props.name: groups
props.doc: Which feet step together: a list of groups of foot indices (each foot in one). Left out, each foot alone.

props.name: lead
props.doc:
How far ahead along the body's motion a step aims past where home will be when it lands, in seconds of that
motion (half a second by default), never more than `reach`: a slow walk takes short steps, a fast one lands a
whole `reach` ahead so the foot spends its time under the body evenly before and behind.

props.name: settle
props.doc: Below this distance from home a still body's foot is left where it is; above it, it steps home to stand square.

props.name: twist
props.doc:
Radians the body may turn from where it faced when a foot landed before that counts as the whole `reach`
(so turning on the spot steps even when a narrow stance hardly moves the feet).

entries.name: StepBody
entries.doc: The body as the planner sees it: where it stands and faces, and how it moves (per second).

props.name: x
props.doc: Where it stands, along x.

props.name: z
props.doc: Where it stands, along z.

props.name: heading
props.doc: Turned from +z toward +x, radians.

props.name: vx
props.doc: Its speed along x.

props.name: vz
props.doc: Its speed along z.

props.name: turn
props.doc: Radians a second.

entries.name: FootState
entries.doc: Where one foot is in its stepping: planted, or part way through a step.

props.name: at
props.doc: Where the foot stands, or stood when it lifted.

props.name: to
props.doc: Where a foot in the air lands.

props.name: t
props.doc: How far through its step, 0 to 1, or −1 while planted.

props.name: facing
props.doc: Which way the body faced (heading) when the foot last landed, or will face where it lands.

props.name: faced
props.doc: Which way the foot faced when it lifted, so a foot in the air can turn from it to `facing`.

props.name: span
props.doc: Seconds this step takes in the air.

entries.name: Steps
entries.doc:
A footstep planner. Give it the feet and where the body starts, then call `update` each frame with where the body
is now: each foot stays planted until it falls too far from its home under the body, then steps to where the body
is going.

ctor.code: new Steps(feet: StepFoot[], body: StepBody, opts: StepOptions)

props.name: feet
props.doc: Each foot's state, in the order the feet were given.

props.name: opts
props.doc: The options in use, with the defaults filled in.

props.name: taken
props.doc: Steps taken so far, by every foot.

methods.name: home
methods.doc: Where foot i stands under the body, `ahead` seconds along its motion.

signatures.code: home(i: number, b: StepBody, ahead?: number): [number, number]

methods.name: off
methods.doc: How far foot i has fallen (or will have, `ahead` seconds on) from where it should stand under the body: its distance from home plus its turn, as a share of `twist` times `reach`.

signatures.code: off(i: number, b: StepBody, ahead?: number): number

methods.name: turned
methods.doc: Which way foot i faces now: as it landed, or partway round to where it lands.

methods.name: stepping
methods.doc: The foot is in the air.

methods.name: update
methods.doc: Moves the plan on by `dt` with the body now at `b`. Returns each foot's place: x, height above the ground, z.

methods.name: reset
methods.doc: Puts every foot back under the body, planted (after a jump in place, or a new start).

modules.title: Loose parts that swing
modules.doc:
Loose parts that swing after the body: tails, ears, cloaks, plaits. Each
chain is a run of bones, each the child of the one before; its points are
every bone's head and the last bone's tail. The first point is pinned where
the body carries it, and the rest are pulled loosely toward where the move
puts them (`follow`, a compliance: bigger is looser), so they lag, swing and
settle (xpbd.ts). Afterwards each bone is turned to point at the next point,
so the move still shapes the part and the swing rides on top.

  const s = new Swing(sk, FOX_SWING)   // once
  ...pose the move, place the creature...
  s.update(sk, dt)                     // turns the chains' bones

Pure and tested.

entries.name: Chain
entries.doc: One chain of bones that swings: a tail, a plait, one side of a cloak.

props.name: bones
props.doc: The chain's bones by name, from the body outward.

props.name: follow
props.doc: How loosely each point after the first follows the move: one number for all, or one per point.

props.name: bend
props.doc: A soft link from each point to the one after next, so a chain bends but doesn't fold back (compliance).

entries.name: SwingSpec
entries.doc: A creature's loose parts, for `Swing`: the chains that swing and what holds them back.

props.name: parts
props.doc: What swings, for a sentence: "tail", "cloak and plait".

props.name: chains
props.doc: The chains of bones that swing.

props.name: ties
props.doc: Links between chains, as [chain, point, chain, point, compliance]: a cloak's two halves, say.

props.name: body
props.doc: The body, as posed now, as capsules the points stay out of.

props.name: damping
props.doc: How quickly swinging dies away, per second (the solver's 1.5 if left out). Stiff tails driven fast want more, or they ring.

props.name: jump
props.doc: A pinned point that moves further than this in a frame means the creature was moved, not walked: start still.

props.name: after
props.doc: Runs after the bones are turned, before the pose is updated: the elf clears its cloak of the legs.

entries.name: Swing
entries.doc:
Loose parts swinging after a move. It hangs a `SwingSpec`'s chains on the cloth solver (`Xpbd`); pose the skeleton,
then call `update` each frame and it turns the chains' bones to follow.

props.name: sim
props.doc: The solver the chains hang on.

props.name: spec
props.doc: The loose parts it was made for.

methods.name: update
methods.doc: Moves the parts on by `dt` seconds once the move is posed and the creature placed, and turns their bones. Leaves the pose updated.

methods.name: reset
methods.doc: Forgets the motion: the next update starts still, where the move puts everything.

entries.name: between
entries.doc: A capsule between two bones' posed heads (or a ball at one), for `SwingSpec.body`.

signatures.code: between(sk: Skeleton, a: string, b: string, r: number): Capsule

entries.name: MorphTarget
entries.doc:
Morphs (blend shapes) for blobs: a second way to move them, beside bones.
A bone carries its blobs rigidly. A morph gives every blob its own small
change, and a slider says how much of it to take, so a cheek can puff or a
mouth can curl with no bone at all.

A mesh morph only moves points. A blob has a shape too, so each target holds
two things per blob:

- `delta`: how far the center moves (3 numbers), as a mesh morph does;
- `grad`: how the surface round the blob stretches and turns (9 numbers),
  the change in the morph's local 3×3 map, J − I.

With weights w the center is p + Σ w·delta and the blob's covariance goes
through J = I + Σ w·grad, as Σ′ = J Σ Jᵀ. Both add up, so morphs mix, run
backward and overshoot the way mesh morphs do, and Σ′ is always a real
covariance whatever the weights.

A morph is a straight line. A part that must travel round something (an
eyelid over an eye) gets in-between `targets`, reached in turn as the weight
goes from 0 to 1.

props.name: delta
props.doc: How far each blob's center moves: x, y, z per blob.

props.name: grad
props.doc: How each blob's shape changes: the morph's local 3×3 map minus identity, nine per blob.

entries.name: Morph
entries.doc: A blend shape for blobs: a named change of shape, reached as its weight goes from 0 to 1.

props.name: name
props.doc: The morph's name, as files and clips know it.

props.name: targets
props.doc: Reached in turn, evenly spaced, as the weight goes 0 → 1; the last is the full shape.

entries.name: targetFrom
entries.doc:
A target from a map of the rest shape: where each blob's center goes, with
the map's local stretch found by nudging the center `h` each way. `to`
returns null for a blob the morph leaves alone.

signatures.code: targetFrom(rest: Blobs, to: (p: Vec3, i: number) => Vec3 | null, h?: number): MorphTarget

entries.name: shares
entries.doc:
Where a weight sits among a morph's targets: between `from` and `to`
(−1 is the rest shape, before the first target), a share `u` of the way,
carried on in a straight line past either end (u below 0 or over 1).

signatures.code: shares(targets: number, w: number): [from: number, to: number, u: number]

entries.name: applyMorphs

signatures.code: applyMorphs(rest: Blobs, morphs: Morph[], weights: ArrayLike<number>, out: Blobs, mode?: "centers" | "shape"): void

entries.name: targetCount

entries.name: targetWeights
entries.doc:
Each target's weight for the morphs' weights, in the order the morphs list
them: what a glTF file animates. A single-target morph's weight is its
target's; a morph with in-betweens spreads its weight over the two targets
either side of it (`shares`). `applyMorphs` gives the same blobs as adding up
every target times its weight here.

signatures.code: targetWeights(morphs: Morph[], weights: ArrayLike<number>, out?: Float32Array<ArrayBuffer>): Float32Array<ArrayBuffer>

entries.name: morphWeight
entries.doc:
A morph's weight back from its `k` targets' weights, starting at `from`: the
inverse of `targetWeights`. The last target with any weight says which stretch
the morph is on, and that weight says how far along it.

entries.name: SculptPart
entries.doc:
Creatures cut the way the pixel scenes are (voxel.ts): shapes given as
distance functions, one solid disc per surface cell, sun and cast shadows
baked in. What a scene does not need and a creature does is bending: here
every cell is weighted to the bones named on its part by distance, as
body.ts weights its blobs, so a neck or a tail curves without a seam.

Parts in one `group` are treated as one solid: a cell buried inside a
neighbor is never made. Give a part its own group when it swings clear of
the rest (a jaw, a wing), or what it uncovers would be missing.

props.name: shape
props.doc: The part's shape, as a distance function.

props.name: color
props.doc: Color (0–1, sRGB) or color at a surface point given its outward normal.

props.name: bones
props.doc: The bones that move it: each cell is weighted by its distance to each.

props.name: group
props.doc:
Parts in one group cut each other where they overlap; a part that swings clear, like a jaw or a wing, wants its
own.

props.name: glow
props.doc: Unlit: the color as given, for eyes and fire.

props.name: opacity
props.doc: How solid its blobs are, 0–1.

props.name: noShadow
props.doc: Casts no shadow on other parts.

props.name: blend
props.doc: How far its weights spread from each bone, if not the creature's `blend`.

entries.name: SculptSpec
entries.doc: A creature to sculpt: its bones, its parts and how far a cell's weight spreads between bones.

props.name: bones
props.doc: The creature's bones.

props.name: parts
props.doc: Its parts.

props.name: blend
props.doc: How far (in world units) a cell's weight spreads from a bone.

props.name: light
props.doc: The baked light; what is left out comes from `DEFAULT_LIGHT`.

props.name: skirt
props.doc:
How deep (world units) a part's skin goes on inside a neighbor of its group. 0 cuts it off at the neighbor's
surface; a little keeps a neck closed where it meets a turning head.

entries.name: Sculpted
entries.doc:
A body builder for procedural creatures: a skeleton, plus a list of simple
shapes (tapered tubes, ellipsoids, flat sheets, and filled cones for things
like flame), each covered in flat surface blobs and weighted to the bones
named on it by distance. The fox (creature.ts) was the first creature and
builds its own way; the frog, elf and dragon are written in this.

Blobs are spread by area, so a part gets its share of `count`; `density`
gives small parts (eyes, claws) more than their share. Lighting is baked into
the color from a fixed light, as for the fox, unless a part is `glow`.

props.name: partOf
props.doc: Which part each blob came from.

props.name: spacing
props.doc: The grid's cell size it was cut at.

entries.name: DISC
entries.doc:
A creature's discs are wider than a scene's (voxel.ts `disc`): a creature is seen as blobs, without pixel mode's
alpha cut, and at the scene's size its far side showed through between them.

entries.name: buildSculpt
entries.doc: Cuts the creature on a grid of `spacing`.

entries.name: sculptToCount
entries.doc:
Cuts the creature at the spacing that gives about `count` blobs. Cells go
roughly as 1 / spacing², but not exactly (thin parts are fattened to the
grid), so it measures twice: a coarse cut, then one nearer the answer, each
a fraction of the final cut's cost. `make` is handed the spacing so thin
parts can be kept at least a cell thick.

signatures.code: sculptToCount(make: (spacing: number) => SculptSpec, count: number, probe?: number): Sculpted

entries.name: toCount
entries.doc: `cut` at the spacing that gives about `count` blobs, for anything cut on a grid (a sculpt, a scene's creature).

signatures.code: toCount<T extends { blobs: Blobs }>(cut: (spacing: number) => T, count: number, probe: number): T

entries.name: joinBuilt
entries.doc: One creature from two builds on the same bones (a sculpted body and a fuzzy flame, say): `b`'s blobs follow `a`'s.

signatures.code: joinBuilt(a: { blobs: Blobs; skin: Skin }, b: { blobs: Blobs; skin: Skin }): { blobs: Blobs; skin: Skin; from: number }

entries.name: smooth
entries.doc: Shapes melted into each other over a distance `k`, so a neck runs into a chest without a crease.

entries.name: flatten
entries.doc: A shape squashed front to back (along z) about z = `at`, to `f` of its depth: a chest, a foot.

signatures.code: flatten(s: Shape, f: number, at?: number): Shape

entries.name: membrane
entries.doc: A skin of thickness 2r stretched over triangles: a wing's membrane, a fin.

entries.name: scales
entries.doc:
A pattern of scales: space cut into staggered cells of size `a`. Gives how
far the point is from its cell's middle (0 at the middle, 1 at the seam) and
a number 0–1 that is the same all over one scale.

signatures.code: scales(p: ArrayLike<number>, a: number): { out: number; id: number }

entries.name: Creature
entries.doc:
A body builder for procedural creatures: a skeleton, plus a list of simple
shapes (tapered tubes, ellipsoids, flat sheets, and filled cones for things
like flame), each covered in flat surface blobs and weighted to the bones
named on it by distance. The fox (creature.ts) was the first creature and
builds its own way; the frog, elf and dragon are written in this.

Blobs are spread by area, so a part gets its share of `count`; `density`
gives small parts (eyes, claws) more than their share. Lighting is baked into
the color from a fixed light, as for the fox, unless a part is `glow`.

props.name: blobs
props.doc: The blobs in the rest pose.

props.name: skin
props.doc: Which bones move each blob, and by how much.

props.name: skeleton
props.doc: The bones, and their pose.

entries.name: Part
entries.doc: One part of a body for `buildBody`: a shape, its color and the bones that move it.

props.name: shape
props.doc: A tube, a ball, a sheet or a filled cone.

props.name: color
props.type: Vec3 | ((p: Vec3, n: Vec3, u: number) => Vec3)
props.doc: Color at a point on the surface, given its outward normal and `u`, how far along a tube or fill (0–1).

props.name: bones
props.doc: The bones that move it, nearest first is not needed: each blob is weighted by its distance to each.

props.name: density
props.doc: Blobs per unit area, relative to the rest.

props.name: size
props.doc: Blob size, relative to the rest.

props.name: opacity
props.doc: Opacity, or opacity at a point given how far along it is (as for `color`).

props.name: glow
props.doc: Unlit: the color as given, for eyes and fire.

props.name: blend
props.doc: How far its weights spread from each bone, if not the creature's `blend`: wider for a sheet that must stretch smoothly.

entries.name: BodySpec
entries.doc: A body for `buildBody`: its bones, its parts and how far a blob's weight spreads between bones.

props.name: bones
props.doc: The body's bones.

props.name: parts
props.doc: Its parts.

props.name: blend
props.doc: How far (in world units) a blob's weight spreads from a bone: about a tenth of a limb.

entries.name: Built
entries.doc:
A body builder for procedural creatures: a skeleton, plus a list of simple
shapes (tapered tubes, ellipsoids, flat sheets, and filled cones for things
like flame), each covered in flat surface blobs and weighted to the bones
named on it by distance. The fox (creature.ts) was the first creature and
builds its own way; the frog, elf and dragon are written in this.

Blobs are spread by area, so a part gets its share of `count`; `density`
gives small parts (eyes, claws) more than their share. Lighting is baked into
the color from a fixed light, as for the fox, unless a part is `glow`.

props.name: partOf
props.doc: Which part each blob came from.

props.name: seen
props.doc: How much of each baked lamp a blob can see, four bytes a blob (voxel.ts `lamps`); left out, every lamp is seen.

props.name: glow
props.doc: How much of its own light each blob gives, a byte a blob (the engine's `Actor.glow`): 255 for a voxel scene's `glow` parts; left out, nothing glows.

entries.name: rng
entries.doc:
A small seeded random number generator: it returns a function that gives the next number from 0 up to 1, the same
run for the same seed.

entries.name: boneTail
entries.doc: Where a bone ends in the rest pose: its tail, else its first child's head, else a short way on from its parent.

entries.name: shapeArea
entries.doc: About how much surface a body shape has, which decides its share of the blobs.

entries.name: buildBody
entries.doc:
Builds a creature from its spec with about `count` blobs. The same spec and
seed always give the same creature.

signatures.code: buildBody(spec: BodySpec, count: number, seed?: number): Built

entries.name: segDist
entries.doc: Distance from p to the segment ab.

signatures.code: segDist(p: ArrayLike<number>, a: Vec3, b: Vec3): number

entries.name: mirror
entries.doc: Mirrors a point (or a list of them) to the creature's other side.

entries.name: spots
entries.doc: A cheap, smooth-ish pattern in 0–1 for spots and scales: the same at the same point every time.

signatures.code: spots(p: Vec3, freq: number, seed?: number): number

entries.name: mix
entries.doc: The point part of the way from `a` to `b`: `t` 0 is `a`, 1 is `b`.
entries.type: (a: Vec3, b: Vec3, t: number) => Vec3

entries.name: Fur
entries.doc:
Fur for a sculpted creature (sculpt.ts): strands grown out of its skin.

The cut creature is a shell of round discs, one per grid cell; textured, it
reads as bricks. Fur is what a Gaussian is good at: every strand here is one
long, thin blob that leaves the skin at a slant and lies the way the coat
runs (`flow`), rooted anywhere inside its cell so the grid never shows. The
shell stays underneath, a shade darker, as the undercoat: it keeps the body
solid where strands part, and the strands' soft tips make the outline soft.

A strand hangs on its root cell's bones with the same weights, so the fur
bends with the body, and it is still a plain blob: files, sprite sheets and
Shape Shifter take it as they take any other.

props.name: length
props.doc: How long a strand is, in world units.

props.name: flow
props.doc: Which way the coat lies at a surface point. Only its part along the skin counts.

props.name: lift
props.doc: How far strands stand up from the skin, in radians: 0 lies flat.

props.name: wild
props.doc: How far strands stray from the flow, in radians either way.

props.name: density
props.doc: Strands here for each strand on plain fur of the same area (a ruff is thicker).

props.name: long
props.doc: A factor on the length at a surface point: a ruff that grows longer toward the chest.

props.name: under
props.doc: How dark the undercoat (the shell under the strands) is, as a share of its color.

props.name: color
props.doc: Strand color at a point, if not the skin's own (a pale tip on dark fur). Lit as the skin under it is.

entries.name: FurryPart
entries.doc: A part of a sculpted creature that may grow fur.

props.name: fur
props.doc: The fur that grows on it; left out, bare skin.

entries.name: quatFromAxes
entries.doc: The rotation whose x, y and z axes are the given (orthonormal, right-handed) columns.

signatures.code: quatFromAxes(x: Vec3, y: Vec3, z: Vec3): Quat

entries.name: growFur
entries.doc:
Grows `total - shell.blobs.count` strands over the furred parts of `shell`
(cut from `parts`, in the same order), spread by area and `density`, so the
creature comes out at exactly `total` blobs. The same shell and parts always
grow the same fur.

signatures.code: growFur(shell: Sculpted, parts: FurryPart[], total: number): Sculpted

entries.name: ZOO
entries.doc: Every creature on the Creature page, simplest first.

entries.name: Move
entries.doc: One of a creature's moves, as a function of time, recorded into a clip when the creature is made.

props.name: name
props.doc: The clip's name in a file.

props.name: label
props.doc: Its name on the page.

props.name: doing
props.doc: What the creature is doing, for the view's description: "jumping on the spot".

props.name: seconds
props.doc: How long one loop takes.

props.name: fps
props.doc: Keys a second when it is recorded as a clip.

props.name: pose
props.doc: Poses the skeleton `t` seconds into the move.

entries.name: Species
entries.doc: A procedural creature the Creature page can show.

props.name: id
props.doc: Its id in addresses and lists.

props.name: name
props.doc: "frog": used in sentences.

props.name: blurb
props.doc: One line for the page.

props.name: detail
props.doc: Blob counts on the detail chips, and the one picked first.

props.name: start
props.doc: The blob count picked first.

props.name: looks
props.doc: Its looks, the first the default.

props.name: make
props.doc: Builds it with about `count` blobs in a look.

props.name: moves
props.doc: Its moves, the first played first.

props.name: view
props.doc: Where the camera starts.

props.name: seed
props.doc: For a made-up monster, the seed that makes it again.

props.name: swing
props.doc: Loose parts (a tail, ears, a cloak) that swing after the body when it's played live (swing.ts); files and sheets keep the move as it is.

entries.name: makeFox
entries.doc: Builds the fox with about `count` blobs: a sculpted skin under strands of fur. `look` picks its coat.

signatures.code: makeFox(count?: number, look?: string): { blobs: Blobs; skin: Skin; skeleton: Skeleton }

entries.name: FOX
entries.doc: The fox as a `Species`: how to build it, its looks, its moves and where the camera starts.

modules.title: Frog
modules.doc:
A frog, sitting, facing +z: twenty bones, including a jaw and a tongue of
three. The tongue lies along the floor of the mouth, rooted at the back;
flicking it grows it straight out between the jaws, so it never stretches
its blobs thin.

entries.name: makeFrog
entries.doc: Builds the frog with about `count` blobs. `look` picks its colors.

signatures.code: makeFrog(count?: number, look?: string): { blobs: Blobs; skin: Skin; skeleton: Skeleton }

entries.name: FROG
entries.doc: The frog as a `Species`: how to build it, its looks, its moves and where the camera starts.

modules.title: Elf
modules.doc:
An elf, standing, facing +z: a humanoid of 29 bones (a spine of three, a
neck and head, arms with hands and fingers, legs with feet and toes, a plait
of hair and a cloak of two each side). The Creature page, Forest Walk and
Dungeon Run's hero are all this one elf.

entries.name: makeElf
entries.doc: The detailed elf, at exactly `count` blobs. `bones` may add to the elf's own (the hero's sword and orb).

signatures.code: makeElf(count?: number, look?: string, bones?: Bone[]): { blobs: Blobs; skin: Skin; skeleton: Skeleton }

entries.name: ELF
entries.doc: The elf as a `Species`: how to build it, its looks, its moves and where the camera starts.

modules.title: Dragon
modules.doc:
A dragon, standing, facing +z, about eight units nose to tail: 43 bones.
Its body is cut the way the pixel scenes are (sculpt.ts): every scale, tooth
and horn ring is a shape or a pattern on one, lit and shadowed once, and
weighted to the bones so the neck and tail still curve. Its wings are skin
stretched between an arm and three finger bones, so the membrane follows
the fingers as they spread and fold.

Its fire is bones too: a chain of six from inside the mouth. In the rest
pose the flame is built FLAME times smaller than life, hidden in the mouth,
so a file opened elsewhere shows a dragon with its mouth shut; breathing
fire grows the first fire bone by FLAME (a scale key, which glTF has) and
the chain unrolls and flickers. Nothing about it is a particle system.

entries.name: makeDragon
entries.doc:
Builds the dragon with about `count` blobs, a small share of them the fire that waits in its mouth. `look` picks
its colors.

signatures.code: makeDragon(count?: number, look?: string): { blobs: Blobs; skin: Skin; skeleton: Skeleton }

entries.name: DRAGON
entries.doc: The dragon as a `Species`: how to build it, its looks, its moves and where the camera starts.

modules.title: Monsters from a seed
modules.doc:
Make me a monster: a creature drawn up from a seed. The seed picks a body
plan (two, four or six legs; how long, how round, how tall), a head (one to
three eyes, a snout, horns, ears or feelers), a tail, back spikes and a
coat and what its hide is (fur in strands, scales, or smooth wet skin), then
cuts it with sculpt.ts like the hand-made zoo. Every monster can
walk on the spot, stand and breathe, and roar, and the same seed always
makes the same monster, so a link can share one.

Monsters face +z and stand on the floor (y = 0) at rest.

entries.name: makeMonster
entries.doc: Builds the monster a seed gives, with about `count` blobs: the same seed always gives the same monster.

signatures.code: makeMonster(seed: number, count?: number): { blobs: Blobs; skin: Skin; skeleton: Skeleton }

entries.name: monsterSpecies
entries.doc: The seed as a creature for the Creature page and its sprite sheets.

entries.name: MAX_SEED
entries.doc: Seeds run from 1 to this; the button picks one and a link may name any.

entries.name: SceneDoc
entries.doc:
A pixel-art scene written as data: no code, so it can be typed by hand, kept
in a file, or written by Claude from a prompt (docs/scene-descriptions.md).
`checkScene` says what is wrong with one, in words that point at the place;
`compileScene` turns a sound one into what the voxel builder, the bones and
pixel mode need.

Units: about 1 is a small house, and a whole scene is about 4 across. y is up, the ground is y = 0, and the
camera starts on the +z side. Colors are '#rrggbb'.

props.name: name
props.doc: The scene's name.

props.name: loop
props.doc: Seconds before everything repeats: 4 to 60.

props.name: light
props.type: { from?: Vec3; ambient?: number; shadow?: number; ramp?: number; crevice?: number; wear?: number; bounce?: number }
props.doc:
The baked sun: `from` points toward it. `ramp` (0–1, 0.7 when left out) turns shade toward cool violet and full
sun toward warm yellow, as a painter's ramp does; `crevice` (0.5) darkens corners and cracks; `wear` (0.5)
lightens sharp outer edges. 0 turns any of them off. `bounce` (off unless set) lets surfaces throw their color onto
what faces them, as a red wall warms the floor beside it; it costs build time, so use it where it shows.

props.name: palette
props.doc: The colors the picture is drawn in, 2 to 32.

props.name: sky
props.doc: The sky behind, top and bottom. Left out, the background is clear.

props.name: skyReach
props.doc: How far down the picture the sky's blend runs before it is all the bottom color: 0.05 to 1, the whole way when left out.

props.name: look
props.type: { dither?: number; glow?: number; outline?: boolean; edges?: boolean; steps?: boolean }
props.doc:
The pixel look it asks for: how much dither and glow, and whether to draw an outline and edge lines. `steps` paints
the scene in steps of its palette as it is cut (each blob takes one palette color, a step of its own paint from shade
to sun), so shade falls in flat bands; left out, shading is smooth and the picture is matched to the palette pixel by pixel.

props.name: disc
props.doc:
How wide each surface disc is, as a share of the grid: 0.4 to 1, 0.55 when left out. Small discs keep paint
crisp but let about a tenth of what lies behind a surface show through; a subject whose far side or inner
parts are much darker or lighter than its near side (a head over an open jaw) wants 0.75, as creatures use.

props.name: camera
props.doc: Where the view starts. `swing` rocks it gently from side to side by that many degrees, once a loop.

props.name: bones
props.doc: Things that move. The land itself needs none: parts with no bone stand still.

props.name: parts
props.doc: Everything in the scene, each a shape with its paint.

props.name: moves
props.doc: What moves, each a whole number of times a loop.

props.name: lights
props.doc: Live lights, at most four: they light what is near them, frame by frame.

props.name: air
props.doc: What hangs in the air: distance haze, low mist, beams of light and drifting specks.

props.name: cover
props.doc:
Snow, moss or dust laid over everything once it is cut (parts marked `bare` and glowing ones keep their paint):
`snow` settles on tops open to the sky, `moss` creeps over shut-in and up-turned faces in patches, `dust` lies
thin on every upturned face. `amount` 0 to 1, from a dusting to most of what faces up.

props.name: focus
props.doc: Where the eye goes: within `r` of `at` the scene is cut at full detail, further out on a grid twice as coarse, in about a quarter of the blobs.

entries.name: AirDoc
entries.doc: A scene's air: haze, mist, shafts of light and specks.

props.name: haze
props.type: { color: string; from?: number; to?: number }
props.doc: Things far from the camera fade toward `color`: it starts `from` units past the view's target (0 when left out) and would be total at `to` (4).

props.name: mist
props.doc: Low banks of mist that drift slowly to and fro, at most four.

props.name: shafts
props.doc: Beams of light, as from a window or a gap in the leaves, at most six: what they land on is lit by them.

props.name: specks
props.doc: Swarms of small things, each moving on its own, at most eight swarms and 300 specks in all.

entries.name: MistDoc
entries.doc: One bank of mist.

props.name: at
props.doc: The middle of the bank.

props.name: half
props.doc: Half its size along x, y (its depth) and z.

props.name: color
props.doc: Its color.

props.name: thick
props.doc: How thick it is, 0 to 1 (0.5 when left out).

entries.name: ShaftDoc
entries.doc: One beam of light.

props.name: from
props.doc: Where it starts (a window, a crack, a lamp) and where it lands.

props.name: to
props.doc: Where it lands.

props.name: r
props.doc: How wide it is, as a radius.

props.name: color
props.doc: Its color.

props.name: strength
props.doc: How bright, 0 to 1 (0.6 when left out).

entries.name: SpeckKind
entries.doc:
What a swarm does: `dust` hangs and twinkles, `embers` rise and fade, `rain` falls fast as streaks, `snow` falls
slowly and sways, `leaves` flutter down, `fireflies` wander and blink, `bubbles` rise and wobble.

entries.name: SpeckDoc
entries.doc: One swarm of specks: dust, embers, rain, snow, leaves, fireflies or bubbles.

props.name: kind
props.doc: What they are, which sets how they move.

props.name: count
props.doc: How many.

props.name: from
props.doc: Two opposite corners of the box they live in: rain and snow fall from its top to its bottom, embers and bubbles rise from its bottom to its top.

props.name: to
props.doc: The box's opposite corner.

props.name: colors
props.doc: Each speck takes one of these.

props.name: size
props.doc: A speck's radius; left out, a size that suits the kind.

props.name: glow
props.doc: Whether they give off light; left out, embers and fireflies do.

props.name: land
props.doc: Rain, snow and leaves only: each lands on whatever stands still under it (or the box's floor), lies a while and goes, then falls again.

props.name: wind
props.doc: Rain, snow and leaves only: how far the wind carries each sideways over its whole fall, [x, z]; rain slants along it.

entries.name: BoneDoc
entries.doc: One bone of a scene: something for parts to ride on and moves to turn.

props.name: name
props.doc: What parts and moves call it.

props.name: at
props.doc: The point it turns and grows about.

props.name: parent
props.doc: Another bone it rides on (named earlier in the list).

entries.name: PartDoc
entries.doc: One part of a scene: a shape, its paint and the bone that carries it.

props.name: shape
props.doc: Its shape.

props.name: paint
props.doc: Its paint.

props.name: bone
props.doc: The bone that carries it; left out, it is part of the land.

props.name: glow
props.doc: Gives off light and takes none: lamps, fire, stars, anything that must stay bright.

props.name: noShadow
props.doc: Casts no shadow: thin things in the air.

props.name: grime
props.doc: A color that gathers in its corners and cracks, as moss or soot does.

props.name: bare
props.doc: Takes none of the scene's `cover`: water, glass, a fresh fire.

props.name: touches
props.doc: Meets other parts by design as it moves (foam round a bobbing buoy): the check for parts passing through each other lets it.

props.name: ink
props.doc:
Little drawn marks over it, one in some 4-by-4 blocks of pixels, never repeating: `hatch`, `stipple`, `cracks`,
`grain` (wood), `tufts` (grass) or `scales`. `amount` (0.5) is the share of blocks marked; `color` the ink, a
darker step of the paint when left out.

props.name: glass
props.type: { see?: number; mirror?: number; top?: boolean }
props.doc:
Water, ice or glass: it shows what lies behind it (`see`, 0.6) and mirrors what is over it (`mirror`, 0.3, more
at a glancing look), painted for the scene's own camera. Its paint tints what shows through, and where the line
from the eye leaves it with nothing met, a darker step of it shows, as the bottom of a pond does. `top` keeps it
to upturned faces, for a pond cut as one slab with earth sides.

props.name: strokes
props.doc: Dabs that follow the form: 0 to 1, how far each cell is drawn as a stroke along the level line round the shape. Shows as brushwork in the Blobs view.

entries.name: ShapeDoc
entries.doc:
